title: Storytelling and Cultural Preservation
description: Preserving indigenous knowledge through oral storytelling and community engagement.
imageDescription: Children gathered under a tree listening to elders tell stories of the forest.
fullDescription: Storytelling is at the heart of NASCEC's mission to preserve indigenous knowledge and cultural heritage. This workshop brought together elders and children from the community to share stories about the forest, its significance, and the wisdom embedded in local folklore. The children learned about the importance of protecting sacred groves, the medicinal value of native trees, and the role of storytelling in passing down environmental stewardship from one generation to the next. Through interactive sessions, the children were encouraged to retell the stories in their own words, ensuring that the oral traditions remain alive and relevant. This initiative strengthens the bond between generations and reinforces the community's commitment to conservation.

title: Tree Follow-up: Weeding and Tending at Musunji
description: Ensuring the survival and growth of trees through consistent care and maintenance.
imageDescription: Community members and students weeding around young trees at Musunji Comprehensive School.
fullDescription: Tree planting is only the beginning of the journey. To ensure the survival and healthy growth of the trees planted at Musunji Comprehensive School, NASCEC organized a follow-up exercise focused on weeding and tending. Community members, students, and NASCEC field officers came together to clear invasive weeds, apply mulch, and check the health of the young trees. This activity is part of NASCEC's commitment to long-term environmental stewardship. By caring for the trees, participants learn about the importance of consistent maintenance, the role of weeding in reducing competition for nutrients and water, and the value of patience in ecological restoration. The exercise also provided an opportunity for the school community to reflect on the progress made since the initial planting and to celebrate the growing green space on their compound.
